sources.notes: Vendor evidence for least-required access, policy/approval, escalation, deployment feedback, and generalized field learning.

sources.title: What a service is
sources.notes: Public-service guidance used for the durable idea that a service delivers an outcome across paths, not merely through an interface.

sources.title: Zero Trust Architecture
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: NIST SP 800-207 supports resource-focused, explicitly authorized access rather than implicit network trust.

sources.title: NIST Privacy Framework Version 1.0
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: Risk- and outcome-based privacy framework used to reinforce organizational ownership and contextual risk decisions; not legal advice.

sources.title: Understand users and their needs
sources.notes: Government service-standard guidance used for whole-problem and context-first discovery; transfer requires judgment.

sources.title: Start by learning user needs
sources.notes: Guidance for interviewing and observing real users, reviewing existing evidence, and treating opinions as assumptions until tested.

sources.title: Introduction to designing government services
sources.notes: High-governance service guidance used for end-to-end, front-to-back, cross-channel, and secure-by-design discovery questions.

sources.title: Map a user's whole problem
sources.notes: Official guidance used for whole-journey mapping and broken handoffs; it does not prescribe one notation.

sources.title: Business Process Model and Notation Version 2.0.2
sources.notes: Versioned formal process-modeling notation cited as one optional representation, not a mandatory discovery method.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.notes: Used narrowly to ground the distinction between transport-level method semantics and workflow-level completion/intent.

sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
sources.notes: First-party engineering pattern used to show that caller intent and ambiguous completion are workflow concerns; no quantitative outcome claim.

sources.title: Using data to improve your service: an introduction
sources.notes: Official service guidance for defining performance data early and understanding use across segments; examples remain public-service specific.

sources.title: Measuring service benefits
sources.notes: Official guidance for baselining and monitoring benefit evidence to support continue, change, or stop decisions; does not establish causal attribution alone.

sources.title: Measuring user satisfaction
sources.notes: Official guidance used for continuous satisfaction and dropout evidence; satisfaction is one signal, not proof of workflow value.

sources.title: Service Level Objectives
sources.notes: First-party engineering book chapter used for user-relevant indicators/objectives tied to action and tradeoffs; practices require contextual adaptation.

sources.title: Morgan Stanley uses AI evals to shape the future of financial services
sources.notes: Vendor/customer story used only for an attributed adoption figure and evaluation practice; outcomes are not independently verified.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
sources.notes: Provider guidance used for provider-neutral tradeoff questions across operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, and sustainability.

sources.title: What is the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
sources.notes: Provider guidance used as a question set for reliability, security, cost, operations, and performance tradeoffs, not proof of architecture quality.

sources.title: The C4 model for visualising software architecture
sources.notes: Official method documentation used for hierarchical context/container abstractions and notation/tool independence; responsibility/trust/failure annotations are book additions.

sources.title: Architecture design principles
sources.notes: Provider architecture guidance used for provider-neutral questions about failure, operations, identity, and recovery; examples are not mandatory.

sources.title: Cloudflare outage on February 20, 2026
sources.notes: First-party postmortem used for configured versus operational state and distributed recovery; all facts remain attributed to Cloudflare.

sources.title: Deep dive into Cloudflare's September 12 dashboard and API outage
sources.notes: First-party postmortem used for control-plane/data-plane separation, request amplification, capacity, and observability; facts remain attributed.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification 3.2.0
sources.notes: Versioned specification for machine-readable HTTP API descriptions; description does not guarantee semantic correctness or operation.

sources.title: AsyncAPI Specification 3.0.0
sources.notes: Versioned protocol-agnostic specification for message-driven interfaces; does not replace domain semantics or operational delivery design.

sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
sources.notes: Versioned schema vocabulary for structural validation; structural validity is not semantic or business validity.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Data quality model
sources.notes: Official standard record used for the existence and scope of a structured-data quality model; copyrighted standard text is not reproduced.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.notes: Versioning specification used only where a public API is declared; it does not solve deployment or data compatibility by itself.

sources.title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.notes: RFC 9700 used as the current OAuth 2.0 security best current practice where OAuth is actually used; not a universal identity design.

sources.title: Cloudflare incident on October 30, 2023
sources.notes: First-party postmortem used for break-glass/recovery dependency questions; it does not justify weakening routine controls.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: Voluntary, use-case-agnostic lifecycle risk framework cited by version; NIST revision activity was active at the research cutoff.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: NIST AI 600-1 used for generative-AI risk prompts organized around govern, map, measure, and manage; requires workflow tailoring.

sources.title: Evals
sources.notes: Volatile vendor documentation used for portable dataset/evaluation concepts; the specific platform was scheduled for late-2026 deprecation.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.notes: First-party engineering guidance for task, trial, grader, transcript, outcome, harness, suite, capability, and regression distinctions.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.notes: First-party engineering guidance used for simple composable workflows, ground truth, checkpoints, and stopping conditions; not a neutral standard.

sources.title: Production ML systems
sources.notes: First-party education/practice source used for the model-as-one-component production-system principle.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026
sources.notes: Community security guide used as a current threat-discovery prompt, not a formal standard or complete threat model.

sources.title: Deployment simulation: Stress testing models in deployment-like contexts
sources.notes: First-party research article used for the limits of static evaluation and deployment-like simulation; simulation still cannot reproduce all production tails.

sources.title: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: Outcome-oriented cybersecurity framework used by version for governance and risk conversations; it does not prescribe or certify a complete implementation.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Framework Version 1.1
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.notes: NIST SP 800-218 final Version 1.1 used for integrating secure software practices into the lifecycle; a later revision was draft at the research cutoff.

sources.title: Application Security Verification Standard
sources.notes: ASVS 5.0.0 used as versioned application-security verification criteria; scope and level remain contextual owner decisions.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation
sources.notes: Official standard record used only for scope/version and the existence of a product-quality model; copyrighted requirements are not reproduced.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.notes: W3C Recommendation used for versioned, testable web accessibility criteria; conformance does not by itself establish complete usability or accessibility for every context.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
sources.notes: Volatile provider guidance used only for the provider-neutral principle that production quality spans interacting operational, security, reliability, performance, cost, and sustainability concerns.

sources.title: Architecture design principles
sources.notes: Volatile provider guidance used for contextual failure, operations, identity, and self-healing design questions; Azure examples are not required architecture.

sources.title: Release Engineering
sources.notes: First-party engineering book chapter used for automation, consistency, reproducibility, and release process principles; large-scale Google practice requires adaptation.

sources.title: Monitoring ML systems
sources.notes: First-party education/practice source used for monitoring data and model quality in addition to service health; workflow metrics and thresholds remain contextual.

sources.title: Agent evals
sources.notes: Volatile vendor documentation used only for portable trace/behavior evaluation concepts; specific interfaces are replaceable.

sources.title: Safety best practices
sources.notes: Volatile vendor guidance used for layered safeguards, testing, monitoring, and human review; not a system-specific risk assessment or guarantee.
